items.text: Understand what SSH is and why it is used to connect to Linux EC2 instances
Know the three SSH connection methods: EC2 Instance Connect, SSH terminal (.pem), and PuTTY (.ppk)
Know that RDP uses port 3389 and is used exclusively for Windows EC2 instances
Understand the difference between Stopping and Terminating an EC2 instance
Know all EC2 instance states: Pending, Running, Stopping, Stopped, Rebooting, Shutting-down, Terminated
Understand the billing implications of each EC2 state (Running = billed, Stopped = EBS only, Terminated = no charge)
Know the five EC2 pricing models and when to use each
Understand Termination Protection and Stop Protection and when to enable them
Successfully connected to a Linux EC2 instance using EC2 Instance Connect (browser method)
Successfully connected using SSH from terminal with chmod 400 on the .pem key
Successfully converted a .pem file to .ppk using PuTTYgen and connected via PuTTY
Retrieved a Windows EC2 Administrator password and connected via RDP
Changed an EC2 instance type by stopping the instance, applying the change, and restarting
Enabled Termination Protection and Stop Protection on an EC2 instance
Can troubleshoot SSH connection failures (Security Group, key permissions, instance state)
Can identify the correct port numbers for SSH (22) and RDP (3389) from exam questions
Know that chmod 400 is required on .pem files and PuTTY requires .ppk format
Can distinguish Reboot (same host, same IP) from Stop/Start (new IP, possibly new host)
Understand that Spot Instances can be interrupted with 2 minutes notice but save up to 90%
Know that Reserved Instances offer up to 72% savings for 1 or 3-year commitments
Can correctly answer Shared Responsibility Model questions about EC2 OS patching
